findings.summary: The stage order is written as a flat list of eight names, so a learner cannot see it as a sequence or see which stages are cheap and fast.
findings.evidence: "Checkout Install Lint Test Build Package Staging Production"
findings.fix: Draw it as a left-to-right flow with arrows, and mark the cheap fast checks (Lint, Test) as run first.

findings.summary: The `needs:` rule is shown only as prose, and the stage-order page never ties the `needs:` fan-in to its YAML.
findings.evidence: "needs: orders jobs; without it jobs run in parallel" followed by `needs: [test, deploy-staging]`
findings.fix: Add a small diagram of test and deploy-staging feeding into deploy-prod, with an approval gate before it.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "operating", "strategy").
findings.evidence: Pass config with env:, secrets.NAME and the matrix: strategy for running across versions or operating systems
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The minimal workflow YAML leaves out the `on:` trigger, so the page's example is not a complete workflow and relies on a separate prose line to finish it.
findings.evidence: "Add on: [push] above jobs:" and the yaml block that starts at "jobs:"
findings.fix: Put `on: [push]` as the first line of the yaml block and delete the "Add on: [push] above jobs:" line.

findings.summary: One bullet holds two ideas, parallel execution and runner assignment.
findings.evidence: "Jobs run in parallel, each on its own runner (runs-on: ubuntu-latest)"
findings.fix: Split it into "Jobs run in parallel" and "Each job gets its own runner: runs-on: ubuntu-latest".

findings.summary: The pyramid table uses 'Coverage' to mean how much of the system a test touches, but page 4 uses 'coverage' for the share of code executed by tests.
findings.evidence: Coverage | Narrow | Wider | Broadest
findings.fix: Rename the page 1 row to 'Scope' (page 6 already uses 'Scope') so 'coverage' only means code coverage.

findings.summary: One table row holds two ideas, cost and flakiness, so a skimmer cannot tell which value belongs to which.
findings.evidence: Cost, flakiness | Low | Medium | High
findings.fix: Split it into a 'Cost' row and a 'Flakiness' row.

findings.summary: The over-mocking code is shown before the idea it illustrates, and the 'Assert behaviour' takeaway appears only after it.
findings.evidence:
python
assert order.total == 42  # output: good
db.save.assert_called_once()  # internal: avoid
check what the code returns or does
Assert behaviour
findings.fix: Put the one-line rule 'Assert outputs, not internal calls' before the code block and drop the repeated takeaway after it.

findings.summary: The Login > Add to cart > Pay > Confirm flow appears without a label tying it to the E2E level, and the 'Failures' row reads ambiguously.
findings.evidence:
Login
Add to cart
Pay
Confirm; Failures | precise | realistic | most realistic
findings.fix: Caption the flow 'E2E example: checkout'. Replace the 'Failures' row with clearer rows, for example 'Pinpoints the cause' and 'Realism'.

findings.summary: The word 'Floor on new code' appears as an orphan label before the closing sentence repeats it, and the coverage-limits bullets run several ideas together.
findings.evidence:
Check test strength with mutation testing: Stryker, mutmut
Floor on new code
Use coverage to find gaps, not as a goal. Enforce a floor on new code.
findings.fix: Remove the stray label. Split the closing sentence into 'Use coverage to find gaps' and 'Enforce a floor on new code'.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet introduces unexplained 70/20/10 shares and orders the gate checks differently from page 5, which says to run fast checks first.
findings.evidence:
Unit | ~70% | Isolated and fast; Tests
Lint
Types
Coverage
Merge; lint, types, then coverage
findings.fix: Mark the shares as a rough guide and order the gate flow Lint, Types, Tests, Coverage, Merge to match page 5.

findings.summary: The strategy table's 'safer ↓' ordering is ambiguous, and blue-green's blast radius does not say what happens after the switch.
findings.evidence: Strategy (safer ↓) | Blast radius | Cost ... Blue-green | 0% until switch | ~2x, the most ... Canary | 1-5% | small extra slice
findings.fix: Drop the 'safer ↓' label or sort by blast radius. Write blue-green as '0% until switch, then 100%' (or 'instant full switch') so the comparison is clear.

findings.summary: The kubectl commands are shown as a bare code block with no one-line statement of what they do.
findings.evidence:
3. Commands
bash
kubectl set image deploy/app app=img:v2
kubectl rollout status deploy/app
kubectl rollout undo deploy/app
kubectl rollout history deploy/app
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code, or comment each line: deploy v2, watch progress, revert, list revisions.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "combinations", "unreachable").
findings.evidence: Mistake: flag debt. Release flags left in the code create dead branches and untested combinations. Remove them after full rollout, and give every flag an owner and expiry date. Also set a safe default for when the flag service is unreachable.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The Common Mistake section is a dense prose paragraph that holds several ideas instead of one-line bullets.
findings.evidence: DROP COLUMN, NOT NULL without default or a type change in the same release as the code leaves rollback no schema. Ship additive migrations first and separately; drop or narrow columns only in a later release, once no running code uses them.
findings.fix: Split it into short bullets: list the risky changes (DROP COLUMN, NOT NULL without default, type change), then 'Why: rollback needs the old schema', then 'Rule: additive first, drop or narrow in a later release'.

findings.summary: The resource code appears before the one-line idea that explains it. An unexplained annotation also sits between the code and the bullets.
findings.evidence:
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "logs" {...} resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "p" {...}
first address: aws_s3_bucket.logs
findings.fix: State the idea first, for example 'A reference to another resource creates an implicit dependency and sets the order', then show the code. Turn the annotation into a labelled callout on the reference line.

findings.summary: One bullet holds two separate ideas, variables and outputs.
findings.evidence: variable takes inputs, output exposes values: reusable config
findings.fix: Split into 'variable: takes inputs' and 'output: exposes values'.

findings.summary: Three interview question-and-answer pairs are run together in one paragraph, so a skimmer can't tell where one answer ends and the next starts.
findings.evidence: No hand-edit or Git? Plaintext secrets, and edits desync state from reality. Locking? Stops two concurrent applies. -/+ ? Destroy first: risk to a database or disk.
findings.fix: Put each question and answer on its own line, as pages 1, 2 and 4 do.

findings.summary: Two bullets each hold two ideas.
findings.evidence: terraform plan is a read-only preview; terraform apply executes it
findings.fix: Use one bullet for plan being a read-only preview and one for apply executing it. Likewise split 'Shares state across a team and locks it' into sharing and locking.

findings.summary: The Fit column of the environments table is ambiguous. Both directory and module setups say 'prod', and workspaces say 'light only', which doesn't say what each setup is good for.
findings.evidence:
Directory per env | separate | prod
Module + -var-file=prod.tfvars | separate | prod
Workspaces | shared backend + config | light only
findings.fix: Replace the Fit values with meaningful labels, for example 'Isolated prod and dev' for the first two rows and 'Light, non-prod only' for workspaces. Or rename the column 'Isolation' and put the guidance in a clear sentence.

findings.summary: The State Tools bullets each hold several commands and ideas, which hurts scanning on the cheat sheet.
findings.evidence:
state rm stops managing; state mv renames, no recreate
plan -refresh-only previews drift; apply -refresh-only records it
findings.fix: Turn these into a Command | Effect table like page 4's, or put one command per bullet.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "something", "expensive").
findings.evidence: Comparison: metrics tell you THAT something is wrong, traces tell you WHERE, and logs tell you WHY. Metrics are cheapest to store; logs are the most expensive at volume.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The outline's trace-ID propagation point is never taught, so a learner cannot explain how a trace follows a request between services.
findings.evidence: Page 1 only says "Spans sharing one trace ID" and "Follows one request across services". The outline's Interview Point asks "what is a trace ID and how does it propagate between services?"
findings.fix: Add a line to the Three Signals section saying the trace ID is generated at the entry point and passed to each downstream call in a request header (for example W3C traceparent). Each service then tags its spans with that ID.

findings.summary: The signals table has an empty Cost cell for traces, so the cost comparison is incomplete.
findings.evidence: "Cost | Cheapest | – | Highest at volume"
findings.fix: Fill in the traces cost, for example "Medium (sampled)", or drop the row.

findings.summary: The YAML example is a fixed-threshold alert, but the page argues for burn-rate alerts over thresholds, and the code appears without a one-line idea stating that.
findings.evidence: expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.01 (shown after "Page: 1h and 5m both above ~14x")
findings.fix: Add a one-line caption that this is the simple threshold form with for:, or replace the example with a multi-window burn-rate expression.

findings.summary: One bullet packs three separate metric definitions, and the blameless bullet mixes report contents with a principle.
findings.evidence: "Track MTTD detect, MTTA acknowledge, MTTR recover"; "Blameless: timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, what went well"
findings.fix: Split into one bullet per metric, or use a small table with columns Metric | Measures, and separate the postmortem sections from the blameless principle.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet calls the three telemetry types "Pillar", while page 1 calls them "signals", and "signals" also names the golden signals. The word "page" also means both a notification and a doc page.
findings.evidence: "Pillar | Tells you" vs page 1 "The Three Signals"; "Every page needs a runbook and an owner"
findings.fix: Use one term for logs/metrics/traces consistently, for example "telemetry type", and write "every paging alert needs a runbook and an owner".

gaps: Containers and Docker images as the deployable artifact
Container orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes) that rolling, blue-green and canary deployments run on
Version control branching strategies such as trunk-based development
overlaps: Cheat sheets: every chapter ends with one
Rollback and zero-downtime database migrations appear in both deployment-strategies and monitoring-rollback
Quality gates and flaky tests in testing-stages overlap with pipeline stages in pipelines
Common mistakes sections repeated across chapters
Environments appear in both pipelines and infrastructure-as-code
